info.title: im-services-analytics API
info.description:
REST APIs exposed by the IM Services Analytics module (package org.selco.e4h) of the eGov DIGIT platform. This service computes SLA breaches, triggers CO2/carbon-emission batch calculations, and sends daily/weekly SLA escalation e-mails for the Incident Management (IM) domain.

Authentication mechanism actually found in this codebase: there is NO servlet Filter, Interceptor, or Spring Security configuration in im-services-analytics, so none of the endpoints in this service enforce authentication themselves. Where a request body is present, it follows the standard eGov convention of embedding a `RequestInfo` object (field name `RequestInfo` in JSON) that carries `authToken` (the Bearer JWT obtained from egov-user OAuth login) and `userInfo` (uuid, userName, roles, etc). This service does not itself validate `authToken`/`userInfo` on incoming requests, but forwards the same `RequestInfo` object downstream (to egov-user/HRMS, MDMS, workflow, filestore, etc.) so that those services can authenticate/authorize the call. Several endpoints (`GET /v1/update_phc`, `POST /v1/carbon/trigger`, `GET /v1/escalation-emails/health`) accept no body/`RequestInfo` at all and are intended to be invoked internally (e.g. by a Kubernetes CronJob) with no bearer-token check. Standard errors raised via `org.egov.tracer.model.CustomException` (egov-tracer 2.9.0-SNAPSHOT, `tracer.detailed.tracing.enabled=true`) are rendered by egov-tracer's default exception handling as HTTP 400 with the `ErrorRes` envelope shown below. Some controller methods additionally catch generic `Exception` themselves and return a plain-text HTTP 500 body instead of the JSON `ErrorRes` shape -- this is called out per-endpoint below.

post.summary: Compute and update SLA for tickets
post.description: Triggers SLA (Service Level Agreement) computation for the tenant identified in the request body, optionally transforming records and optionally including closed tickets. Delegates to PrioritySLAService.computeAndUpdateSLA(...). Returns a plain-text confirmation message on success. NOTE: this endpoint catches all internal exceptions itself and returns a plain-text HTTP 500 body (not the JSON ErrorRes envelope) -- only request-body validation failures (bean validation on SLARequest, via @Valid) surface as the standard egov-tracer 400 ErrorRes shape.

parameters.description: Whether to transform/re-map ticket data as part of SLA computation.

parameters.name: closedtickets
parameters.description: Whether to include already-closed tickets in the SLA computation.

post.description: HTTP trigger intended for a Kubernetes CronJob (same pattern as the RMS service's POST /v1/trigger). Runs CarbonEmissionBatchService.process(...) for the given tenant/month/year. If month and year are not both supplied, the calculation runs for the last fully-completed calendar month. If tenantId is not supplied, the properties-configured default tenant (co2.default.tenant.id, e.g. "in") is used. No request body -- an internal RequestInfo is synthesized in code with msgId="co2-cron-trigger" and all other fields null/empty. Any exception is NOT caught by the controller, so it propagates to egov-tracer's default exception handling.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Tenant to run the CO2 calculation for. Defaults to the configured co2.default.tenant.id (e.g. "in") when omitted.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: 1-12 calendar month to compute for. Must be supplied together with year, otherwise the last completed month is used.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: 4-digit calendar year to compute for. Must be supplied together with month, otherwise the last completed month is used.

post.summary: Run daily SLA-breach escalation e-mail processing
post.description: For every active EscalationRecipient defined in MDMS (Incident.EscalationRecipient), finds users matching the recipient's role and boundary level (state or country), queries SLA-breach tickets per configured escalation level (LEVEL_ZERO/LEVEL_ONE/LEVEL_TWO), uploads a CSV per level to FileStore, updates Elasticsearch escalation state, and publishes a role-based escalation e-mail per user onto Kafka (egov-notification-mail contract). Intended to be invoked once per day by a scheduler/CronJob. NOTE: this endpoint catches all internal exceptions itself (and also publishes a failure status via EscalationStatusService) and returns a plain-text HTTP 500 body -- it does NOT return the JSON ErrorRes envelope on failure.

post.summary: Run weekly SLA/DRE system report escalation e-mail processing
post.description: For every active EscalationRecipient defined in MDMS (Incident.EscalationRecipient), determines relevant tenants/states per recipient, generates per-tenant weekly report data, builds one consolidated CSV across all mapped states (uploaded to FileStore under tenantId "in"), and sends one consolidated weekly-report e-mail per unique recipient e-mail address via Kafka. Intended to be invoked once a week (Monday 09:00 IST) by a scheduler/CronJob. NOTE: this endpoint catches all internal exceptions itself (and also publishes a failure status via EscalationStatusService) and returns a plain-text HTTP 500 body -- it does NOT return the JSON ErrorRes envelope on failure.

Role.description: org.egov.common.contract.request.Role -- role assigned to a user, scoped to a tenant.

UserInfo.description: org.egov.common.contract.request.User -- authenticated user info embedded in RequestInfo.

RequestInfo.description: org.egov.common.contract.request.RequestInfo -- standard eGov DIGIT request envelope carrying request metadata and the caller's auth token/user info. This IS the authentication mechanism for this service's endpoints that accept it: there is no separate Authorization header check, authToken is a Bearer JWT (obtained via egov-user OAuth login) that this service forwards to downstream services.

authToken.description: Bearer JWT obtained from egov-user OAuth login.

ResponseInfo.description: org.egov.common.contract.response.ResponseInfo -- standard eGov response envelope. Used inside ErrorRes; this service's success responses are plain-text strings, not ResponseInfo-wrapped JSON.

Error.description: org.egov.tracer.model.Error -- single error entry inside an ErrorRes, as produced by egov-tracer's default exception handling for CustomException and framework exceptions.

message.example: Failed to fetch CO2 emission factors from MDMS

description.example: Failed to fetch CO2 emission factors from MDMS for tenantId in

ErrorRes.description: Standard egov-tracer error envelope, returned with HTTP 400 for CustomException (and, depending on tracer configuration, other HTTP statuses for other uncaught exceptions). Field names ResponseInfo/Errors are capitalized to match egov-tracer's JSON convention.

AuditDetails.description: Collection of audit related fields used by most models.

Incident.description: Instance of a service request raised for a particular facility/service. Any one of 'address' or '(lat and lng)' or 'addressid' is mandatory (per upstream API contract, not enforced by bean validation on this model beyond the fields marked required).

phcSubType.description: JSON property name is phcSubType; Java field is 'phcsubtype'.

comments.example: Test incident for audit pipeline verification

IncidentRequest.description: Request object to publish/test an incident onto the audit-records processing pipeline. Used by POST /v1/test_update_phc.

EscalationEmailRequest.description: Request body for the escalation e-mail trigger endpoints (POST /v1/escalation-emails/daily and /weekly). Carries only RequestInfo -- there is no additional payload; all recipients/tickets are resolved server-side from MDMS, workflow, and Elasticsearch.
